newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU outlaws 30 mln marks aid paid to Bestwood GmbH.
newsitem.headline: EU outlaws 30 mln marks aid paid to Bestwood GmbH.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had banned 30 million marks in subsidies paid to east German fibreboard company Bestwood GmbH because the local authorities who provided the aid failed to request EU approval.
It also warned the authorities -- the state of Mecklenberg- Vorpommern -- against granting any new, unauthorised aid.

The Commission said it started a probe into the case in November 1995 after it received complaints from unnamed competitors about the payment of a 5.0-million-mark loan and a guarantee worth 25 million marks to Bestwood.
Bestwood, which was once Germany's largest maker of fibre and particle boards, has gone bankrupt since the Commission opened its probe.

The Commission said in a statement it was aware there was a potential buyer for Bestwood on the condition that the loss-making company received more subsidies. But it warned that under EU state aid rules covering the region the aid should not go beyond 35 percent of the overall investment.

The Commission has become very tough about public money paid to ailing businesses in the former east Germany after turning a blind eye to huge subsidies paid by the federal government to the east in the years that followed reunification in 1990.
